title: The main kinds of writing systems
examples: What kinds of writing systems are there?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: What does each symbol stand for?

explain.say: Did you know there are different kinds of writing, not just different letters? It all depends on what each symbol stands for. Look at the board. The first group is alphabets: Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Korean Hangul. In an alphabet, symbols stand for single sounds, vowels and consonants.

explain.say: Now look at the second group: abjads, like Arabic and Hebrew. They mainly write the consonants, and readers fill in the short vowels. Can you read this: bnn? Banana!

explain.say: The third group is abugidas, like Devanagari, Tamil, Thai and Amharic. Each consonant comes with a built-in vowel, and small marks change it. Ka becomes ki with one little sign. Have you seen any of these scripts?

explain.say: Last group: syllabaries, like Japanese kana. One symbol stands for a whole syllable. Look at the board: su, shi. Sushi is written with just two kana, one for each syllable. Can you guess how many kana your name would need?

explain.say: Super! One more kind: logographic, like Chinese, where a symbol stands for a word or meaning. And look at the board: Hangul, invented in Korea in the 1400s, groups its letters into syllable blocks. Challenge: which kind of script is your own language written in?

faq.q: What kinds of writing systems are there?
faq.a: The main kinds are alphabets, abjads, abugidas, syllabaries and logographic systems. They differ in what each symbol stands for: a sound, a consonant, a syllable or a word.
A syllabary uses one symbol for each syllable. Japanese hiragana and katakana are syllabaries, and so is the Cherokee script.
Yes. Hangul has letters for consonants and vowels, but it stacks them into square blocks, one block per syllable. It was created in the 1440s under King Sejong.

faq.q: What is the difference between an abjad and an abugida?
faq.a: An abjad writes mainly consonants and often leaves vowels out, like Arabic. An abugida writes consonants with a built-in vowel and marks to change it, like Devanagari.

faq.q: Does Japanese use more than one script?
faq.a: Yes. Japanese mixes kanji, characters borrowed from Chinese, with two syllabaries, hiragana and katakana, and sometimes Latin letters too.

facts: Hangul was created in Korea in the 1440s under King Sejong the Great.
Japanese writing mixes three scripts: kanji, hiragana and katakana.
The Cherokee syllabary was created by Sequoyah in the early 1800s.
